citations.relevance: Addresses functions unlisted in Table 1004.1.3.

Where a building contains two or more occupancies, the means of egress requirements shall apply to each portion of the building based on the occupancy of that space. Where two or more occupancies utilize portions of the same means of egress system, those egress components shall meet the more stringent requirements of all occupancies that are served. Section BC 1005: Means of Egress Sizing

1004.3 1004.3 Fixed seating. For areas having fixed seats and aisles, the occupant load shall be determined by the number of fixed seats installed therein. The occupant load for areas in which fixed seating is not installed, such as waiting spaces, shall be determined in accordance with Section 1004.1.3 and added to the number of fixed seats. The occupant load of wheelchair spaces and the associated companion seat shall be based on one occupant for each wheelchair space and one occupant for the associated companion seat provided in accordance with Section 1108.2.3. For areas having fixed seating without dividing arms, the occupant load shall be not less than the number of seats based on one person for each 18 inches (457.2 mm) of seating length. The occupant load of seating booths shall be based on one person for each 24 inches (609.6 mm) of booth seat length measured at the backrest of the seating booth.

1004.1 1004.1 Design occupant load. Design occupant load. In determining means of egress requirements, the number of occupants for whom means of egress facilities shall be provided shall be established by the largest number computed in accordance with Section 1004.1.3, unless otherwise permitted by Section 1004.1.3.1, 1004.1.3.2 or 1004.2.

1004.1.2 1004.1.2 Multiple function occupant load. Where an area under consideration contains multiple functions having different occupant load factors, the design occupant load for such area shall be based on the floor area of each function calculated independently.

1004.1.3.2 1004.1.3.2 Unlisted functions. Where data regarding the square feet area per person for a function is not listed in Table 1004.1.3 , the occupant load shall be established by a registered design professional, subject to the approval of the commissioner.

1004.1.3.1 1004.1.3.1 Modifications. Where the actual number of occupants of any space will be significantly lower than listed in Table 1004.1.3 , the commissioner may establish a lower basis for the determination of the number of occupants.

1004.1.1.2.3 1004.1.1.2.3 Group R-2 accessory spaces as primary function on a story. Where the aggregate Group R-2 occupancy accessory area of all rooms, areas or spaces, including outdoor spaces that are not provided with independent means of egress and that do not converge into interior means of egress, exceed 50 percent of the building area of the story in which they are located, and the total number of occupants on such story exceeds 150 persons, the following conditions shall apply: 1. The interior corridors or portions thereof serving such accessory spaces shall be constructed as public corridors in accordance with Table 1020.1.2 with 1-hour fire-resistance-rated fire barriers, and 2-hour fire-resistance-rated fire barriers where a dead-end corridor exceeds 40 feet (12 192 mm) in length; 2. Access to the corridors shall be limited to those necessary for exit access through the corridor from normally occupied spaces. Direct openings from the mechanical, electrical and other storage spaces shall not be permitted, except that access to the corridor may be provided through a vestibule constructed with fire barriers, with a minimum fire-resistance rating consistent with the required hourly rating for the corridor; 3. Corridors or portions thereof serving such accessory spaces shall be sufficient to accommodate a total occupant load on the basis of 3 square feet (0.28 m 2 ) per person; 4. The minimum dimension of such corridors shall be sufficient to accommodate the total occupant load discharging into such corridors, but shall in no case be less than 5 feet (1524 mm) in minimum dimension; and 5. In addition to Conditions 1 through 4 above, one of the following conditions shall be met: 5.1. Each of the interior exit stairways and ramps serving such story shall be protected by a smokeproof enclosure in accordance with Section 909.20; 5.2. The corridor or portions of the corridor serving the rooms, areas or spaces that are accessory to the Group R-2 occupancy shall be pressurized in accordance with requirements that are applicable to interior exit stairways. Connecting interior exit stairways need not be pressurized unless otherwise required by this code; 5.3. All passenger elevators serving the rooms, areas, or spaces that are accessory to the Group R-2 occupancy shall comply with occupant self-evacuation elevator requirements in Section 3008.1 through 3008.11; or 5.4. One additional exit stairway meeting the requirements of Sections 1009 and 1023 shall be provided in addition to the minimum number of exits required by Section 1006 . The total width of any combination of remaining exit stairways with one exit stairway removed shall not be less than the total width required by Section 1005.3. Rooms, areas or spaces that do not comply with the conditions in Sections 1004.1.1.2.1 and 1004.1.1.2.2, or Section 1004.1.1.2.3 where applicable, shall have occupant loads calculated cumulatively per story and be classified as Occupancy Group A.

1004.1.1.2 1004.1.1.2 Cumulative occupant loads in Group R-2 occupancies. Rooms, areas or spaces that are accessory to a Group R-2 occupancy and that comply with the conditions below may have occupant loads calculated individually per room, area, or space, and be classified as Occupancy Group R-2.

1004.1.1.1 1004.1.1.1 Cumulative occupant loads for interconnected spaces. Where the path of egress travel includes intervening rooms, areas or spaces, cumulative occupant loads shall be determined in accordance with this section.

CERTIFICATE OF OPERATION. A certificate issued by the department upon satisfactory inspection of a specific piece of hoisting equipment to ensure that the equipment is in compliance with this code. DWELLING UNIT. A single unit consisting of one or more habitable rooms and occupied or arranged to be occupied as a unit separate from all other units within a dwelling. EXIT ACCESS. That portion of a means of egress system that leads from any occupied portion of a building or structure to an exit. FIXED SEATING. Furniture or fixture designed and installed for the use of sitting and secured in place including bench-type seats and seats with or without backs or arm rests. INTERIOR EXIT STAIRWAY. An exit component that serves to meet one or more means of egress design requirements, such as required number of exits or exit access travel distance, and provides for a protected path of egress travel to the exit discharge or public way. OCCUPANT LOAD . The number of persons for which the means of egress of a building or portion thereof is designed . PARKING GARAGE. A structure or portion of a structure, other than a private garage or carport, used for the parking or storage of motor vehicles. WHEELCHAIR SPACE . A space for a single wheelchair and its occupant .

answer.answerText:
**64 occupants combined** under the stipulated 2022 NYC BC Table 1004.1.3 functions.

- **Business office:** 2,400 gross sq ft ÷ **100 gross sq ft/occupant** = **24 occupants**.
- **Assembly room—without fixed seats, unconcentrated tables and chairs:** 600 net sq ft ÷ **15 net sq ft/occupant** = **40 occupants**.
- **Combined occupant load:** 24 + 40 = **64 occupants**.

The table assigns the office and no-fixed-seat assembly functions different factors, and each function must be calculated independently. The stipulated assembly room uses the table’s **“Assembly without fixed seats—Unconcentrated (tables and chairs)”** factor—not the office factor. (BC §§ 1004.1.2, 1004.1.3)

Because the stipulated room has no fixed seats, the fixed-seating calculation does not apply; areas without fixed seating are determined under Table 1004.1.3. (BC § 1004.3)

If occupants from both spaces pass through the same intervening or accessory egress space, that shared portion is designed for their cumulative **64-person** load. (BC §§ 1004.1.1.1, 1004.1.1.1.1) Means-of-egress requirements apply to each portion based on its occupancy, and a shared component must meet the more stringent requirements of the occupancies it serves. (BC § 1004.5)

The supplied table expressly lists both stipulated functions, so the unlisted-function procedure is not used. The supplied Group R-2 cumulative-load provisions address spaces accessory to Group R-2 and therefore do not alter this stipulated office-and-assembly calculation. (BC §§ 1004.1.3.2, 1004.1.1.2, 1004.1.1.2.3)
answer.conclusion: **64 occupants combined** under the stipulated 2022 NYC BC Table 1004.1.3 functions.

supportedPoints.heading: Separate factors produce a 64-person combined load
supportedPoints.explanation: Table 1004.1.3 assigns business areas 100 gross square feet per occupant and assembly spaces without fixed seats having unconcentrated tables and chairs 15 net square feet per occupant. BC § 1004.1.2 requires functions having different factors to be calculated independently. Thus: 2,400 gross square feet ÷ 100 = 24 occupants; 600 net square feet ÷ 15 = 40 occupants; and 24 + 40 = 64 occupants. BC § 1004.1 establishes the design occupant load for means-of-egress purposes using the Section 1004.1.3 computation, subject to its stated alternatives.

supportedPoints.heading: No-fixed-seat table entry governs the assembly room
supportedPoints.explanation: BC § 1004.3 applies its seat-count method to areas having fixed seats and aisles; it directs areas without fixed seating to Section 1004.1.3. Because the hypothetical specifies no fixed seats, the Table 1004.1.3 entry for assembly without fixed seats—unconcentrated tables and chairs—governs the 600-net-square-foot assembly-room calculation.

supportedPoints.heading: Shared egress carries the cumulative load
supportedPoints.explanation: Where the egress path includes intervening rooms, areas, or spaces, cumulative loads are determined under BC § 1004.1.1.1. Where occupants egress through other spaces, the design occupant load at that point is the combined load of the interconnected accessory or intervening spaces. Thus, a shared egress portion used by both stipulated spaces carries 64 occupants.

supportedPoints.heading: Multiple-occupancy egress scope
supportedPoints.explanation: Means-of-egress requirements apply to each portion of a building according to that space’s occupancy. A component shared by two or more occupancies must meet the more stringent requirements of all occupancies served.

supportedPoints.heading: Unlisted-function procedure is not used
supportedPoints.explanation: BC § 1004.1.3.2 applies when a function’s square-feet-per-person data is not listed in Table 1004.1.3. Both stipulated functions are expressly listed in the table, so their listed factors control this calculation.

supportedPoints.heading: Group R-2 cumulative-load provisions do not apply to this stipulated scenario
supportedPoints.explanation: BC § 1004.1.1.2 addresses rooms, areas, or spaces accessory to a Group R-2 occupancy, and BC § 1004.1.1.2.3 establishes additional conditions where aggregate Group R-2 accessory areas are the primary function on a story. The stipulated ordinary business office and separate assembly room are not described as Group R-2 accessory spaces, so those provisions do not change the stated calculation.

citations.title: 1004.1.2 Multiple function occupant load.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1004.1.2 1004.1.2 Multiple function occupant load. Where an area under consideration contains multiple functions having different occupant load factors, the design occupant load for such area shall be based on the floor area of each function calculated independently.

citations.relevance: Requires independent calculation of functions with different occupant-load factors.

citations.title: 1004.1 Design occupant load.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1004.1 1004.1 Design occupant load. Design occupant load. In determining means of egress requirements, the number of occupants for whom means of egress facilities shall be provided shall be established by the largest number computed in accordance with Section 1004.1.3, unless otherwise permitted by Section 1004.1.3.1, 1004.1.3.2 or 1004.2.

citations.relevance: Establishes the design occupant-load framework for means of egress.

citations.title: 1004.3 Fixed seating.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1004.3 1004.3 Fixed seating. For areas having fixed seats and aisles, the occupant load shall be determined by the number of fixed seats installed therein. The occupant load for areas in which fixed seating is not installed, such as waiting spaces, shall be determined in accordance with Section 1004.1.3 and added to the number of fixed seats. The occupant load of wheelchair spaces and the associated companion seat shall be based on one occupant for each wheelchair space and one occupant for the associated companion seat provided in accordance with Section 1108.2.3. For areas having fixed seating without dividing arms, the occupant load shall be not less than the number of seats based on one person for each 18 inches (457.2 mm) of seating length. The occupant load of seating booths shall be based on one person for each 24 inches (609.6 mm) of booth seat length measured at the backrest of the seating booth.

citations.relevance: Confirms that a space without fixed seating is calculated under Section 1004.1.3 rather than the fixed-seat method.

citations.title: 1004.1.1.1 Cumulative occupant loads for interconnected spaces.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1004.1.1.1 1004.1.1.1 Cumulative occupant loads for interconnected spaces. Where the path of egress travel includes intervening rooms, areas or spaces, cumulative occupant loads shall be determined in accordance with this section.

citations.relevance: Introduces cumulative-load determination where egress travel includes intervening spaces.

citations.title: 1004.1.1.1.1 Intervening spaces or accessory areas.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1004.1.1.1.1 1004.1.1.1.1 Intervening spaces or accessory areas. Where occupants egress from one or more rooms, areas or spaces through others, the design occupant load shall be the combined occupant load of interconnected accessory or intervening spaces. Design of egress path capacity shall be based on the cumulative portion of occupant loads of all rooms, areas or spaces to that point along the path of egress travel.

citations.relevance: Requires the combined occupant load at shared intervening or accessory egress spaces.

citations.title: 1004.5 Multiple occupancies.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1004.5 1004.5 Multiple occupancies. Where a building contains two or more occupancies, the means of egress requirements shall apply to each portion of the building based on the occupancy of that space. Where two or more occupancies utilize portions of the same means of egress system, those egress components shall meet the more stringent requirements of all occupancies that are served. Section BC 1005: Means of Egress Sizing

citations.relevance: Sets multiple-occupancy egress application and the more-stringent shared-egress rule.

citations.title: 1004.1.3.2 Unlisted functions.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1004.1.3.2 1004.1.3.2 Unlisted functions. Where data regarding the square feet area per person for a function is not listed in Table 1004.1.3 , the occupant load shall be established by a registered design professional, subject to the approval of the commissioner.

citations.relevance: Establishes the procedure for functions not listed in Table 1004.1.3; it is inapplicable because both stipulated functions are listed.

citations.title: 1004.1.1.2 Cumulative occupant loads in Group R-2 occupancies.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1004.1.1.2 1004.1.1.2 Cumulative occupant loads in Group R-2 occupancies. Rooms, areas or spaces that are accessory to a Group R-2 occupancy and that comply with the conditions below may have occupant loads calculated individually per room, area, or space, and be classified as Occupancy Group R-2.

citations.relevance: Limits its cumulative-load rule to rooms, areas, or spaces accessory to Group R-2 occupancies.

citations.title: 1004.1.1.2.3 Group R-2 accessory spaces as primary function on a story.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1004.1.1.2.3 1004.1.1.2.3 Group R-2 accessory spaces as primary function on a story. Where the aggregate Group R-2 occupancy accessory area of all rooms, areas or spaces, including outdoor spaces that are not provided with independent means of egress and that do not converge into interior means of egress, exceed 50 percent of the building area of the story in which they are located, and the total number of occupants on such story exceeds 150 persons, the following conditions shall apply: 1. The interior corridors or portions thereof serving such accessory spaces shall be constructed as public corridors in accordance with Table 1020.1.2 with 1-hour fire-resistance-rated fire barriers, and 2-hour fire-resistance-rated fire barriers where a dead-end corridor exceeds 40 feet (12 192 mm) in length; 2. Access to the corridors shall be limited to those necessary for exit access through the corridor from normally occupied spaces. Direct openings from the mechanical, electrical and other storage spaces shall not be permitted, except that access to the corridor may be provided through a vestibule constructed with fire barriers, with a minimum fire-resistance rating consistent with the required hourly rating for the corridor; 3. Corridors or portions thereof serving such accessory spaces shall be sufficient to accommodate a total occupant load on the basis of 3 square feet (0.28 m 2 ) per person; 4. The minimum dimension of such corridors shall be sufficient to accommodate the total occupant load discharging into such corridors, but shall in no case be less than 5 feet (1524 mm) in minimum dimension; and 5. In addition to Conditions 1 through 4 above, one of the following conditions shall be met: 5.1. Each of the interior exit stairways and ramps serving such story shall be protected by a smokeproof enclosure in accordance with Section 909.20; 5.2. The corridor or portions of the corridor serving the rooms, areas or spaces that are accessory to the Group R-2 occupancy shall be pressurized in accordance with requirements that are applicable to interior exit stairways. Connecting interior exit stairways need not be pressurized unless otherwise required by this code; 5.3. All passenger elevators serving the rooms, areas, or spaces that are accessory to the Group R-2 occupancy shall comply with occupant self-evacuation elevator requirements in Section 3008.1 through 3008.11; or 5.4. One additional exit stairway meeting the requirements of Sections 1009 and 1023 shall be provided in addition to the minimum number of exits required by Section 1006 . The total width of any combination of remaining exit stairways with one exit stairway removed shall not be less than the total width required by Section 1005.3. Rooms, areas or spaces that do not comply with the conditions in Sections 1004.1.1.2.1 and 1004.1.1.2.2, or Section 1004.1.1.2.3 where applicable, shall have occupant loads calculated cumulatively per story and be classified as Occupancy Group A.

citations.relevance: Provides the related Group R-2 accessory-space-as-primary-function-on-a-story conditions, which do not apply to the stipulated scenario.

Where a building contains two or more occupancies, the means of egress requirements shall apply to each portion of the building based on the occupancy of that space. The occupant load for areas in which fixed seating is not installed, such as waiting spaces, shall be determined in accordance with Section 1004.1.3 and added to the number of fixed seats. The occupant load of wheelchair spaces and the associated companion seat shall be based on one occupant for each wheelchair space and one occupant for the associated companion seat provided in accordance with Section 1108.2.3. For areas having fixed seating without dividing arms, the occupant load shall be not less than the number of seats based on one person for each 18 inches (457.2 mm) of seating length. 1004.1.2 1004.1.2 Multiple function occupant load. Where an area under consideration contains multiple functions having different occupant load factors, the design occupant load for such area shall be based on the floor area of each function calculated independently.

1004.1.3.2 1004.1.3.2 Unlisted functions. Where data regarding the square feet area per person for a function is not listed in Table 1004.1.3 , the occupant load shall be established by a registered design professional, subject to the approval of the commissioner.

1004.1.1.2.3 1004.1.1.2.3 Group R-2 accessory spaces as primary function on a story. Where the aggregate Group R-2 occupancy accessory area of all rooms, areas or spaces, including outdoor spaces that are not provided with independent means of egress and that do not converge into interior means of egress, exceed 50 percent of the building area of the story in which they are located, and the total number of occupants on such story exceeds 150 persons, the following conditions shall apply: 1. The interior corridors or portions thereof serving such accessory spaces shall be constructed as public corridors in accordance with Table 1020.1.2 with 1-hour fire-resistance-rated fire barriers, and 2-hour fire-resistance-rated fire barriers where a dead-end corridor exceeds 40 feet (12 192 mm) in length; 2. Access to the corridors shall be limited to those necessary for exit access through the corridor from normally occupied spaces. Direct openings from the mechanical, electrical and other storage spaces shall not be permitted, except that access to the corridor may be provided through a vestibule constructed with fire barriers, with a minimum fire-resistance rating consistent with the required hourly rating for the corridor; 3. Corridors or portions thereof serving such accessory spaces shall be sufficient to accommodate a total occupant load on the basis of 3 square feet (0.28 m 2 ) per person; 4. The minimum dimension of such corridors shall be sufficient to accommodate the total occupant load discharging into such corridors, but shall in no case be less than 5 feet (1524 mm) in minimum dimension; and 5. In addition to Conditions 1 through 4 above, one of the following conditions shall be met: 5.1. Each of the interior exit stairways and ramps serving such story shall be protected by a smokeproof enclosure in accordance with Section 909.20; 5.2. The corridor or portions of the corridor serving the rooms, areas or spaces that are accessory to the Group R-2 occupancy shall be pressurized in accordance with requirements that are applicable to interior exit stairways. Connecting interior exit stairways need not be pressurized unless otherwise required by this code; 5.3. All passenger elevators serving the rooms, areas, or spaces that are accessory to the Group R-2 occupancy shall comply with occupant self-evacuation elevator requirements in Section 3008.1 through 3008.11; or 5.4. One additional exit stairway meeting the requirements of Sections 1009 and 1023 shall be provided in addition to the minimum number of exits required by Section 1006 . The total width of any combination of remaining exit stairways with one exit stairway removed shall not be less than the total width required by Section 1005.3. Rooms, areas or spaces that do not comply with the conditions in Sections 1004.1.1.2.1 and 1004.1.1.2.2, or Section 1004.1.1.2.3 where applicable, shall have occupant loads calculated cumulatively per story and be classified as Occupancy Group A.

1004.1.1.2 1004.1.1.2 Cumulative occupant loads in Group R-2 occupancies. Rooms, areas or spaces that are accessory to a Group R-2 occupancy and that comply with the conditions below may have occupant loads calculated individually per room, area, or space, and be classified as Occupancy Group R-2.

1004.1.1.1 1004.1.1.1 Cumulative occupant loads for interconnected spaces. Where the path of egress travel includes intervening rooms, areas or spaces, cumulative occupant loads shall be determined in accordance with this section.

1004.1.1.1.1 1004.1.1.1.1 Intervening spaces or accessory areas. Where occupants egress from one or more rooms, areas or spaces through others, the design occupant load shall be the combined occupant load of interconnected accessory or intervening spaces. Design of egress path capacity shall be based on the cumulative portion of occupant loads of all rooms, areas or spaces to that point along the path of egress travel.

CERTIFICATE OF OPERATION. A certificate issued by the department upon satisfactory inspection of a specific piece of hoisting equipment to ensure that the equipment is in compliance with this code. DWELLING UNIT. A single unit consisting of one or more habitable rooms and occupied or arranged to be occupied as a unit separate from all other units within a dwelling. EXIT ACCESS. That portion of a means of egress system that leads from any occupied portion of a building or structure to an exit. FIXED SEATING. Furniture or fixture designed and installed for the use of sitting and secured in place including bench-type seats and seats with or without backs or arm rests. INTERIOR EXIT STAIRWAY. An exit component that serves to meet one or more means of egress design requirements, such as required number of exits or exit access travel distance, and provides for a protected path of egress travel to the exit discharge or public way. OCCUPANT LOAD . The number of persons for which the means of egress of a building or portion thereof is designed . PARKING GARAGE. A structure or portion of a structure, other than a private garage or carport, used for the parking or storage of motor vehicles. WHEELCHAIR SPACE . A space for a single wheelchair and its occupant .

answer.answerText:
**64 occupants combined** for the stipulated spaces under 2022 NYC BC Table 1004.1.3.

- **Business office:** **100 gross sf/occupant**.
2,400 gross sf ÷ 100 = **24 occupants**.

- **Assembly room—no fixed seats; unconcentrated tables and chairs:** **15 net sf/occupant**.
600 net sf ÷ 15 = **40 occupants**.

- **Combined occupant load:** 24 + 40 = **64 occupants**.

The two functions use distinct table factors and are calculated independently. (BC § 1004.1.2; Table 1004.1.3.) Because the assembly room has no fixed seating, its occupant load is determined under Table 1004.1.3 rather than the fixed-seat method. (BC § 1004.3.)

If these spaces constitute two or more legal occupancies, BC § 1004.5 applies egress requirements by the occupancy of each space, and any shared egress component must meet the more stringent requirements of the occupancies served.
answer.conclusion: **64 occupants combined** for the stipulated spaces under 2022 NYC BC Table 1004.1.3.

supportedPoints.heading: Separate factors produce a 64-person load
supportedPoints.explanation: Table 1004.1.3 assigns business areas 100 gross square feet per occupant and assembly spaces without fixed seats with unconcentrated tables and chairs 15 net square feet per occupant. Section 1004.1.2 requires functions with different factors to be calculated independently. Thus, 2,400 gross square feet ÷ 100 = 24 occupants; 600 net square feet ÷ 15 = 40 occupants; and 24 + 40 = 64 occupants.

supportedPoints.heading: No-fixed-seat assembly factor applies
supportedPoints.explanation: Section 1004.3 directs that areas without fixed seating have their occupant load determined under Section 1004.1.3. The stipulated assembly room therefore uses the table entry for unconcentrated tables and chairs.

supportedPoints.heading: Multiple-occupancy egress rule is conditional
supportedPoints.explanation: If the stipulated spaces constitute two or more occupancies, Section 1004.5 requires means-of-egress requirements to apply to each portion based on its occupancy. A shared egress component must meet the more stringent requirements of all occupancies served.

sources.text: 1004.5 1004.5 Multiple occupancies. Where a building contains two or more occupancies, the means of egress requirements shall apply to each portion of the building based on the occupancy of that space. Where two or more occupancies utilize portions of the same means of egress system, those egress components shall meet the more stringent requirements of all occupancies that are served. Section BC 1005: Means of Egress Sizing

For the purposes of occupant load calculation, permanent fixtures and amenities such as shrubs, decorative pools, non-walkable paving surfaces, etc. may be deducted from the total floor area. c. A rooftop or terrace in Group R-2 or R-3 occupancies that is provided for the incidental, recreational use by the residential tenants residing in the same residential building. d. Where the maximum occupant load of the rooftop or terrace exceeds 74 persons based on occupant load calculations, a Place of Assembly Certificate of Operation is required pursuant to Section 28-117.1 of the Administrative Code and Item 1 of Section 303.7 of this code. e. To be used only when the occupant load for the function of the space is not listed elsewhere in Table 1004.1.3 .

1004.1.2 1004.1.2 Multiple function occupant load. Where an area under consideration contains multiple functions having different occupant load factors, the design occupant load for such area shall be based on the floor area of each function calculated independently.

1004.3 1004.3 Fixed seating. For areas having fixed seats and aisles, the occupant load shall be determined by the number of fixed seats installed therein. The occupant load for areas in which fixed seating is not installed, such as waiting spaces, shall be determined in accordance with Section 1004.1.3 and added to the number of fixed seats. The occupant load of wheelchair spaces and the associated companion seat shall be based on one occupant for each wheelchair space and one occupant for the associated companion seat provided in accordance with Section 1108.2.3. For areas having fixed seating without dividing arms, the occupant load shall be not less than the number of seats based on one person for each 18 inches (457.2 mm) of seating length. The occupant load of seating booths shall be based on one person for each 24 inches (609.6 mm) of booth seat length measured at the backrest of the seating booth.

1004.1 1004.1 Design occupant load. Design occupant load. In determining means of egress requirements, the number of occupants for whom means of egress facilities shall be provided shall be established by the largest number computed in accordance with Section 1004.1.3, unless otherwise permitted by Section 1004.1.3.1, 1004.1.3.2 or 1004.2.

1004.1.3.2 1004.1.3.2 Unlisted functions. Where data regarding the square feet area per person for a function is not listed in Table 1004.1.3 , the occupant load shall be established by a registered design professional, subject to the approval of the commissioner.

1004.1.1.2.3 1004.1.1.2.3 Group R-2 accessory spaces as primary function on a story. Where the aggregate Group R-2 occupancy accessory area of all rooms, areas or spaces, including outdoor spaces that are not provided with independent means of egress and that do not converge into interior means of egress, exceed 50 percent of the building area of the story in which they are located, and the total number of occupants on such story exceeds 150 persons, the following conditions shall apply: 1. The interior corridors or portions thereof serving such accessory spaces shall be constructed as public corridors in accordance with Table 1020.1.2 with 1-hour fire-resistance-rated fire barriers, and 2-hour fire-resistance-rated fire barriers where a dead-end corridor exceeds 40 feet (12 192 mm) in length; 2. Access to the corridors shall be limited to those necessary for exit access through the corridor from normally occupied spaces. Direct openings from the mechanical, electrical and other storage spaces shall not be permitted, except that access to the corridor may be provided through a vestibule constructed with fire barriers, with a minimum fire-resistance rating consistent with the required hourly rating for the corridor; 3. Corridors or portions thereof serving such accessory spaces shall be sufficient to accommodate a total occupant load on the basis of 3 square feet (0.28 m 2 ) per person; 4. The minimum dimension of such corridors shall be sufficient to accommodate the total occupant load discharging into such corridors, but shall in no case be less than 5 feet (1524 mm) in minimum dimension; and 5. In addition to Conditions 1 through 4 above, one of the following conditions shall be met: 5.1. Each of the interior exit stairways and ramps serving such story shall be protected by a smokeproof enclosure in accordance with Section 909.20; 5.2. The corridor or portions of the corridor serving the rooms, areas or spaces that are accessory to the Group R-2 occupancy shall be pressurized in accordance with requirements that are applicable to interior exit stairways. Connecting interior exit stairways need not be pressurized unless otherwise required by this code; 5.3. All passenger elevators serving the rooms, areas, or spaces that are accessory to the Group R-2 occupancy shall comply with occupant self-evacuation elevator requirements in Section 3008.1 through 3008.11; or 5.4. One additional exit stairway meeting the requirements of Sections 1009 and 1023 shall be provided in addition to the minimum number of exits required by Section 1006 . The total width of any combination of remaining exit stairways with one exit stairway removed shall not be less than the total width required by Section 1005.3. Rooms, areas or spaces that do not comply with the conditions in Sections 1004.1.1.2.1 and 1004.1.1.2.2, or Section 1004.1.1.2.3 where applicable, shall have occupant loads calculated cumulatively per story and be classified as Occupancy Group A.

1004.1.1.2 1004.1.1.2 Cumulative occupant loads in Group R-2 occupancies. Rooms, areas or spaces that are accessory to a Group R-2 occupancy and that comply with the conditions below may have occupant loads calculated individually per room, area, or space, and be classified as Occupancy Group R-2.

1004.1.1.1 1004.1.1.1 Cumulative occupant loads for interconnected spaces. Where the path of egress travel includes intervening rooms, areas or spaces, cumulative occupant loads shall be determined in accordance with this section.

1004.1.1.1.1 1004.1.1.1.1 Intervening spaces or accessory areas. Where occupants egress from one or more rooms, areas or spaces through others, the design occupant load shall be the combined occupant load of interconnected accessory or intervening spaces. Design of egress path capacity shall be based on the cumulative portion of occupant loads of all rooms, areas or spaces to that point along the path of egress travel.

CERTIFICATE OF OPERATION. A certificate issued by the department upon satisfactory inspection of a specific piece of hoisting equipment to ensure that the equipment is in compliance with this code. DWELLING UNIT. A single unit consisting of one or more habitable rooms and occupied or arranged to be occupied as a unit separate from all other units within a dwelling. EXIT ACCESS. That portion of a means of egress system that leads from any occupied portion of a building or structure to an exit. FIXED SEATING. Furniture or fixture designed and installed for the use of sitting and secured in place including bench-type seats and seats with or without backs or arm rests. INTERIOR EXIT STAIRWAY. An exit component that serves to meet one or more means of egress design requirements, such as required number of exits or exit access travel distance, and provides for a protected path of egress travel to the exit discharge or public way. answer.answerText:
**No.** A pedestrian ramp that is part of an accessible means of egress is limited to a running slope of **1:12 maximum (8%)**. A **1:8 (12.5%)** running slope exceeds that limit. (BC § 1012.2)

BC § 1012.2 separates ramps used as part of a means of egress or accessible route from “other pedestrian ramps.” Only the latter category may be as steep as 1:8. The stipulated accessible means-of-egress ramp is therefore in the 1:12 category. (BC § 1012.2)

The vehicle-ramp provision does not change that result. Its relief applies only to certain parking-garage vehicle ramps that are not an accessible route serving the stated accessible elements and are not part of an accessible means of egress. (BC § 1012.1, Exception 3)

For the slope question, no project-specific facts are needed. The supplied evidence also establishes separate ramp-design requirements that do not relax the 1:12 limit: means-of-egress ramp width/capacity must meet the corridor requirement and have 36 inches clear width minimum; landings are required at the listed locations; ramps rising more than 6 inches require handrails on both sides; and edge protection is required unless an expressed exception applies. (BC §§ 1012.5.1, 1012.6, 1012.8, 1012.10)

The supplied occupant-load provisions concern calculation of occupants for spaces with differing functions and do not establish an alternate ramp-slope allowance. (BC §§ 1004.1.2, 1004.1.3)
answer.conclusion: **No.** A pedestrian ramp that is part of an accessible means of egress is limited to a running slope of **1:12 maximum (8%)**. A **1:8 (12.5%)** running slope exceeds that limit. (BC § 1012.2)

supportedPoints.heading: Accessible means-of-egress ramp limit is 1:12
supportedPoints.explanation: A ramp used as part of a means of egress or part of an accessible route must have a running slope no steeper than one vertical in 12 horizontal (8%). Thus, the stipulated pedestrian ramp that is part of an accessible means of egress cannot use a 1:8 running slope.

supportedPoints.heading: The 1:8 allowance is for other pedestrian ramps
supportedPoints.explanation: BC § 1012.2 permits a maximum 1:8 (12.5%) slope for “other pedestrian ramps,” a separate category from ramps used as part of a means of egress or accessible route. An accessible means of egress is a continuous and unobstructed way of egress travel from an accessible point to a public way and may include an assisted rescue path.

supportedPoints.heading: Vehicle-ramp exception does not apply
supportedPoints.explanation: Chapter 1012 applies to ramps used as a component of a means of egress. The parking-garage vehicle-ramp exception relieves compliance with specified provisions only where the vehicle ramp is not an accessible route serving the listed accessible elements and is not part of an accessible means of egress. It supplies no 1:8 allowance for the stipulated ramp.

supportedPoints.heading: Related supplied ramp requirements
supportedPoints.explanation: For a means-of-egress ramp, the supplied provisions require corridor-based minimum width and capacity and 36 inches minimum clear width; landings at the bottom and top of each ramp, turns, entrances, exits, and doors; handrails on both sides where rise exceeds 6 inches, except as stated for permitted ramped aisles; and edge protection at ramp runs and applicable landing sides unless a stated exception applies. These provisions do not change the 1:12 running-slope limit.

supportedPoints.heading: Occupant-load provisions do not provide a ramp-slope alternative
supportedPoints.explanation: BC § 1004.1.2 requires floor area for different functions to be calculated independently when they have different occupant-load factors, and BC Table 1004.1.3 supplies maximum floor-area allowances per occupant for areas without fixed seating. Neither provision establishes an alternate slope for a pedestrian ramp in an accessible means of egress.

citations.title: 1012.2 Slope.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.2 1012.2 Slope. Ramps used as part of a means of egress or part of an accessible route shall have a running slope not steeper than one unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (8-percent slope). The slope of other pedestrian ramps shall not be steeper than one unit vertical in eight units horizontal (12.5-percent slope). Exceptions: 1. Aisle ramp slope in occupancies of Group A shall comply with Section 1029.13. 2. In garages three stories or less in height and serving not more than one level below grade, ramps with a maximum slope of one unit vertical in seven units horizontal (14-percent slope) may serve as part of a nonaccessible means of egress.

citations.relevance: Establishes the 1:12 maximum running slope for ramps used as part of a means of egress or accessible route and the separate 1:8 limit for other pedestrian ramps.

citations.title: SECTION 202: Definitions

supportingPassages.selectedText:
ACCESSIBLE MEANS OF EGRESS. A continuous and unobstructed way of egress travel from any accessible point in a building or facility to a public way. Such way of egress travel may include an assisted rescue path.

ACCESSIBLE ROUTE. A continuous, unobstructed path that complies with Chapter 11 .

DWELLING UNIT. A single unit consisting of one or more habitable rooms and occupied or arranged to be occupied as a unit separate from all other units within a dwelling.

EXIT ACCESS. That portion of a means of egress system that leads from any occupied portion of a building or structure to an exit.

FIXED SEATING. Furniture or fixture designed and installed for the use of sitting and secured in place including bench-type seats and seats with or without backs or arm rests.

OCCUPANT LOAD . The number of persons for which the means of egress of a building or portion thereof is designed .

PARKING GARAGE. A structure or portion of a structure, other than a private garage or carport, used for the parking or storage of motor vehicles.

WHEELCHAIR SPACE . A space for a single wheelchair and its occupant .

citations.relevance: Defines accessible means of egress.

citations.title: 1012.1 Scope.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.1 1012.1 Scope. The provisions of this section shall apply to ramps used as a component of a means of egress. Exceptions: 1. Other than ramps that are part of the accessible routes providing access in accordance with Sections 1108.2 through 1108.2.4 and 1108.2.6, ramped aisles within assembly rooms or spaces shall comply with the provisions in Section 1029 . 2. Curb ramps shall comply with ICC A117.1. 3. Vehicle ramps in parking garages for pedestrian exit access shall not be required to comply with Sections 1012.3 through 1012.10 where they are not an accessible route serving accessible parking spaces, other required accessible elements or part of an accessible means of egress.

citations.relevance: Establishes Chapter 1012 scope and the limited parking-garage vehicle-ramp exception.

citations.title: 1012.5.1 Width and capacity.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.5.1 1012.5.1 Width and capacity. The minimum width and required capacity of a means of egress ramp shall be not less than that required for corridors by Section 1020.2. The clear width of a ramp between handrails, if provided, or other permissible projections shall be 36 inches (914.4 mm) minimum.

citations.relevance: Establishes means-of-egress ramp width and capacity requirements.

citations.title: 1012.6 Landings.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.6 1012.6 Landings. Ramps shall have landings at the bottom and top of each ramp, points of turning, entrance, exits and at doors. Landings shall comply with Sections 1012.6.1 through 1012.6.5.

citations.relevance: Establishes required ramp-landing locations.

citations.title: 1012.8 Handrails.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.8 1012.8 Handrails. Ramps with a rise greater than 6 inches (152.4 mm) shall have handrails on both sides. Handrails shall comply with Section 1014 . Exception: Handrails for ramped aisles are not required where permitted by Section 1029.15.

citations.relevance: Establishes the handrail trigger for ramps with more than 6 inches of rise.

citations.title: 1012.10 Edge protection.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.10 1012.10 Edge protection. Edge protection complying with Section 1012.10.1 shall be provided on each side of ramp runs and at each side of ramp landings not adjoining another ramp run or stairway. Exceptions: 1. Edge protection is not required on ramps that are not required to have handrails, provided they have flared sides that comply with the ICC A117.1 curb ramp provisions. 2. Edge protection is not required on the sides of ramp landings having a vertical dropoff of not more than 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) within 10 inches (254 mm) horizontally of the required landing area. 3. Edge protection is not required where the floor or ground surface of the ramp run or landing extends 12 inches (304.8 mm) minimum beyond the inside face of handrail complying with Section 1014 .

citations.relevance: Establishes edge-protection requirements and stated exceptions.

citations.title: 1004.1.2 Multiple function occupant load.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1004.1.2 1004.1.2 Multiple function occupant load. Where an area under consideration contains multiple functions having different occupant load factors, the design occupant load for such area shall be based on the floor area of each function calculated independently.

citations.relevance: Establishes independent calculation for areas with multiple functions and different occupant-load factors; it does not alter the ramp-slope rule.

1004.1.2 1004.1.2 Multiple function occupant load. Where an area under consideration contains multiple functions having different occupant load factors, the design occupant load for such area shall be based on the floor area of each function calculated independently.

1012.2 1012.2 Slope. Ramps used as part of a means of egress or part of an accessible route shall have a running slope not steeper than one unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (8-percent slope). The slope of other pedestrian ramps shall not be steeper than one unit vertical in eight units horizontal (12.5-percent slope). Exceptions: 1. Aisle ramp slope in occupancies of Group A shall comply with Section 1029.13. 2. In garages three stories or less in height and serving not more than one level below grade, ramps with a maximum slope of one unit vertical in seven units horizontal (14-percent slope) may serve as part of a nonaccessible means of egress.

1004.3 1004.3 Fixed seating. For areas having fixed seats and aisles, the occupant load shall be determined by the number of fixed seats installed therein. The occupant load for areas in which fixed seating is not installed, such as waiting spaces, shall be determined in accordance with Section 1004.1.3 and added to the number of fixed seats. The occupant load of wheelchair spaces and the associated companion seat shall be based on one occupant for each wheelchair space and one occupant for the associated companion seat provided in accordance with Section 1108.2.3. For areas having fixed seating without dividing arms, the occupant load shall be not less than the number of seats based on one person for each 18 inches (457.2 mm) of seating length. The occupant load of seating booths shall be based on one person for each 24 inches (609.6 mm) of booth seat length measured at the backrest of the seating booth.

1012.1 1012.1 Scope. The provisions of this section shall apply to ramps used as a component of a means of egress. Exceptions: 1. Other than ramps that are part of the accessible routes providing access in accordance with Sections 1108.2 through 1108.2.4 and 1108.2.6, ramped aisles within assembly rooms or spaces shall comply with the provisions in Section 1029 . 2. Curb ramps shall comply with ICC A117.1. 3. Vehicle ramps in parking garages for pedestrian exit access shall not be required to comply with Sections 1012.3 through 1012.10 where they are not an accessible route serving accessible parking spaces, other required accessible elements or part of an accessible means of egress.

1004.1 1004.1 Design occupant load. Design occupant load. In determining means of egress requirements, the number of occupants for whom means of egress facilities shall be provided shall be established by the largest number computed in accordance with Section 1004.1.3, unless otherwise permitted by Section 1004.1.3.1, 1004.1.3.2 or 1004.2.

1012.10 1012.10 Edge protection. Edge protection complying with Section 1012.10.1 shall be provided on each side of ramp runs and at each side of ramp landings not adjoining another ramp run or stairway. Exceptions: 1. Edge protection is not required on ramps that are not required to have handrails, provided they have flared sides that comply with the ICC A117.1 curb ramp provisions. 2. Edge protection is not required on the sides of ramp landings having a vertical dropoff of not more than 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) within 10 inches (254 mm) horizontally of the required landing area. 3. Edge protection is not required where the floor or ground surface of the ramp run or landing extends 12 inches (304.8 mm) minimum beyond the inside face of handrail complying with Section 1014 .

1012.5.1 1012.5.1 Width and capacity. The minimum width and required capacity of a means of egress ramp shall be not less than that required for corridors by Section 1020.2. The clear width of a ramp between handrails, if provided, or other permissible projections shall be 36 inches (914.4 mm) minimum.

1012.8 1012.8 Handrails. Ramps with a rise greater than 6 inches (152.4 mm) shall have handrails on both sides. Handrails shall comply with Section 1014 . Exception: Handrails for ramped aisles are not required where permitted by Section 1029.15.
1012.6 1012.6 Landings. Ramps shall have landings at the bottom and top of each ramp, points of turning, entrance, exits and at doors. Landings shall comply with Sections 1012.6.1 through 1012.6.5.

ACCESSIBLE MEANS OF EGRESS. A continuous and unobstructed way of egress travel from any accessible point in a building or facility to a public way. Such way of egress travel may include an assisted rescue path. ACCESSIBLE ROUTE. A continuous, unobstructed path that complies with Chapter 11 . DWELLING UNIT. A single unit consisting of one or more habitable rooms and occupied or arranged to be occupied as a unit separate from all other units within a dwelling. EXIT ACCESS. That portion of a means of egress system that leads from any occupied portion of a building or structure to an exit. FIXED SEATING. Furniture or fixture designed and installed for the use of sitting and secured in place including bench-type seats and seats with or without backs or arm rests. OCCUPANT LOAD . The number of persons for which the means of egress of a building or portion thereof is designed . PARKING GARAGE. A structure or portion of a structure, other than a private garage or carport, used for the parking or storage of motor vehicles. WHEELCHAIR SPACE . A space for a single wheelchair and its occupant .
1012.3 1012.3 Cross slope. The slope measured perpendicular to the direction of travel of a ramp shall not be steeper than one unit vertical in 48 units horizontal (2-percent slope).
1012.4 1012.4 Vertical rise. The rise for any ramp run shall be 30 inches (762 mm) maximum.
1012.5 1012.5 Minimum dimensions. The minimum dimensions of means of egress ramps shall comply with Sections 1012.5.1 through 1012.5.3.

1012.7 1012.7 Ramp construction. Ramps shall be built of materials consistent with the types permitted for the type of construction of the building, except that wood handrails shall be permitted for all types of construction.

1012.9 1012.9 Guards. Guards shall be provided where required by Section 1015 and shall be constructed in accordance with Section 1015. Such guards may be used to satisfy the requirement of edge protection of Section 1012.10.

1004.1.3.1 1004.1.3.1 Modifications. Where the actual number of occupants of any space will be significantly lower than listed in Table 1004.1.3 , the commissioner may establish a lower basis for the determination of the number of occupants.

answer.answerText:
**A 1:8 running slope is not permitted under the general rule for a ramp that is part of an accessible means of egress:** the maximum is **1:12 (8%)**. A 1:8 slope is 12.5%. (BC § 1012.2)

BC § 1012.2 reserves the **1:8** maximum for **“other pedestrian ramps,”** separate from ramps used as part of a means of egress or accessible route. However, the supplied text contains a separate exception: an **aisle ramp in a Group A occupancy** must comply with BC § 1029.13. Because the hypothetical does not say whether the ramp is a Group A aisle ramp, that exception cannot be ruled out; its supplied cross-reference text is needed to determine whether 1:8 could be allowed on that distinct path. The other stated exception permits up to 1:7 only for a qualifying garage ramp serving a **nonaccessible** means of egress, so it does not apply to the stipulated accessible means of egress. (BC § 1012.2)

The vehicle-ramp exception is different and does **not** supply a 1:8 slope allowance. It exempts qualifying parking-garage vehicle ramps only from BC §§ 1012.3 through 1012.10—not the running-slope rule in BC § 1012.2—and only where the ramp is neither the specified accessible route nor part of an accessible means of egress. (BC § 1012.1)

The supplied related provisions do not alter that slope result: they address cross slope (1:48 maximum), 30-inch maximum rise per run, landings, slip-resistant securely attached surfaces, handrails for rises over 6 inches subject to the stated ramped-aisle exception, width/capacity, and edge protection subject to its listed exceptions. (BC §§ 1012.3, 1012.4, 1012.5.1, 1012.6, 1012.7.1, 1012.8, 1012.10)
answer.conclusion: **A 1:8 running slope is not permitted under the general rule for a ramp that is part of an accessible means of egress:** the maximum is **1:12 (8%)**. A 1:8 slope is 12.5%. (BC § 1012.2)

supportedPoints.heading: General accessible-egress slope limit
supportedPoints.explanation: Ramps used as part of a means of egress or part of an accessible route must have a running slope no steeper than 1 vertical in 12 horizontal (8 percent). The separate 1:8 maximum is for “other pedestrian ramps.” Thus, absent a stated exception, a 1:8 slope is not permitted for the stipulated accessible means-of-egress ramp.

supportedPoints.heading: Group A aisle-ramp exception remains unresolved
supportedPoints.explanation: BC § 1012.2 directs aisle-ramp slope in Group A occupancies to BC § 1029.13. The supplied evidence does not include that section, and the hypothetical does not establish whether the ramp is a Group A aisle ramp. The separate 1:7 garage exception expressly applies only to a qualifying nonaccessible means of egress.

supportedPoints.heading: Vehicle-ramp exception does not alter the slope rule
supportedPoints.explanation: The parking-garage vehicle-ramp exception applies only to BC §§ 1012.3 through 1012.10, not BC § 1012.2. It also requires that the vehicle ramp not be an accessible route serving the specified accessible elements and not be part of an accessible means of egress.

supportedPoints.heading: Related ramp criteria do not change running-slope limit
supportedPoints.explanation: The supplied provisions separately regulate 1:48 maximum cross slope, 30-inch maximum rise for a run, landing locations, slip-resistant securely attached surfaces, handrails for rises exceeding 6 inches subject to the stated ramped-aisle exception, means-of-egress-ramp width and capacity, and edge protection subject to listed exceptions. They do not replace the BC § 1012.2 running-slope rule.

supportedPoints.heading: Accessibility design framework
supportedPoints.explanation: Buildings and facilities must be designed and constructed to be accessible in accordance with ICC A117.1 and the code. This supplied framework does not itself modify BC § 1012.2’s stated running-slope categories.

However, the supplied text contains a separate exception: an **aisle ramp in a Group A occupancy** must comply with BC § 1029.13. Because the hypothetical does not say whether the ramp is a Group A aisle ramp, that exception cannot be ruled out; its supplied cross-reference text is needed to determine whether 1:8 could be allowed on that distinct path. The other stated exception permits up to 1:7 only for a qualifying garage ramp serving a **nonaccessible** means of egress, so it does not apply to the stipulated accessible means of egress. (BC § 1012.2)

The vehicle-ramp exception is different and does **not** supply a 1:8 slope allowance. It exempts qualifying parking-garage vehicle ramps only from BC §§ 1012.3 through 1012.10—not the running-slope rule in BC § 1012.2—and only where the ramp is neither the specified accessible route nor part of an accessible means of egress. (BC § 1012.1)

The supplied related provisions do not alter that slope result: they address cross slope (1:48 maximum), 30-inch maximum rise per run, landings, slip-resistant securely attached surfaces, handrails for rises over 6 inches subject to the stated ramped-aisle exception, width/capacity, and edge protection subject to its listed exceptions. (BC §§ 1012.3, 1012.4, 1012.5.1, 1012.6, 1012.7.1, 1012.8, 1012.10)

citations.title: 1012.2 Slope.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.2 1012.2 Slope. Ramps used as part of a means of egress or part of an accessible route shall have a running slope not steeper than one unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (8-percent slope). The slope of other pedestrian ramps shall not be steeper than one unit vertical in eight units horizontal (12.5-percent slope). Exceptions: 1. Aisle ramp slope in occupancies of Group A shall comply with Section 1029.13. 2. In garages three stories or less in height and serving not more than one level below grade, ramps with a maximum slope of one unit vertical in seven units horizontal (14-percent slope) may serve as part of a nonaccessible means of egress.

citations.relevance: Establishes the 1:12 maximum for ramps in a means of egress or accessible route, the 1:8 rule for other pedestrian ramps, and the Group A aisle-ramp and nonaccessible-garage exceptions.

citations.title: 1012.1 Scope.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.1 1012.1 Scope. The provisions of this section shall apply to ramps used as a component of a means of egress. Exceptions: 1. Other than ramps that are part of the accessible routes providing access in accordance with Sections 1108.2 through 1108.2.4 and 1108.2.6, ramped aisles within assembly rooms or spaces shall comply with the provisions in Section 1029 . 2. Curb ramps shall comply with ICC A117.1. 3. Vehicle ramps in parking garages for pedestrian exit access shall not be required to comply with Sections 1012.3 through 1012.10 where they are not an accessible route serving accessible parking spaces, other required accessible elements or part of an accessible means of egress.

citations.relevance: Establishes the limited scope and conditions of the parking-garage vehicle-ramp exception.

citations.title: 1012.3 Cross slope.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.3 1012.3 Cross slope. The slope measured perpendicular to the direction of travel of a ramp shall not be steeper than one unit vertical in 48 units horizontal (2-percent slope).

citations.relevance: Establishes the 1:48 maximum cross slope.

citations.title: 1012.4 Vertical rise.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.4 1012.4 Vertical rise. The rise for any ramp run shall be 30 inches (762 mm) maximum.

citations.relevance: Establishes the 30-inch maximum rise per ramp run.

citations.title: 1012.5.1 Width and capacity.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.5.1 1012.5.1 Width and capacity. The minimum width and required capacity of a means of egress ramp shall be not less than that required for corridors by Section 1020.2. The clear width of a ramp between handrails, if provided, or other permissible projections shall be 36 inches (914.4 mm) minimum.

citations.relevance: Establishes means-of-egress-ramp width and capacity provisions.

citations.title: 1012.6 Landings.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.6 1012.6 Landings. Ramps shall have landings at the bottom and top of each ramp, points of turning, entrance, exits and at doors. Landings shall comply with Sections 1012.6.1 through 1012.6.5.

citations.relevance: Establishes required landing locations.

citations.title: 1012.7.1 Ramp surface.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.7.1 1012.7.1 Ramp surface. The surface of ramps shall be of slip-resistant materials that are securely attached.

citations.relevance: Establishes ramp-surface criteria.

citations.title: 1012.8 Handrails.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.8 1012.8 Handrails. Ramps with a rise greater than 6 inches (152.4 mm) shall have handrails on both sides. Handrails shall comply with Section 1014 . Exception: Handrails for ramped aisles are not required where permitted by Section 1029.15.

citations.relevance: Establishes handrail requirements and its stated ramped-aisle exception.

citations.title: 1012.10 Edge protection.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1012.10 1012.10 Edge protection. Edge protection complying with Section 1012.10.1 shall be provided on each side of ramp runs and at each side of ramp landings not adjoining another ramp run or stairway. Exceptions: 1. Edge protection is not required on ramps that are not required to have handrails, provided they have flared sides that comply with the ICC A117.1 curb ramp provisions. 2. Edge protection is not required on the sides of ramp landings having a vertical dropoff of not more than 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) within 10 inches (254 mm) horizontally of the required landing area. 3. Edge protection is not required where the floor or ground surface of the ramp run or landing extends 12 inches (304.8 mm) minimum beyond the inside face of handrail complying with Section 1014 .

citations.relevance: Establishes edge-protection requirements and exceptions.

citations.title: 1101.2 Design.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1101.2 1101.2 Design. Buildings and facilities shall be designed and constructed to be accessible in accordance with ICC A117.1 and this code.

citations.relevance: Establishes the general accessibility design framework.

sources.text: 1012.2 1012.2 Slope. Ramps used as part of a means of egress or part of an accessible route shall have a running slope not steeper than one unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (8-percent slope). The slope of other pedestrian ramps shall not be steeper than one unit vertical in eight units horizontal (12.5-percent slope). Exceptions: 1. Aisle ramp slope in occupancies of Group A shall comply with Section 1029.13. 2. In garages three stories or less in height and serving not more than one level below grade, ramps with a maximum slope of one unit vertical in seven units horizontal (14-percent slope) may serve as part of a nonaccessible means of egress.

1012.1 1012.1 Scope. The provisions of this section shall apply to ramps used as a component of a means of egress. Exceptions: 1. Other than ramps that are part of the accessible routes providing access in accordance with Sections 1108.2 through 1108.2.4 and 1108.2.6, ramped aisles within assembly rooms or spaces shall comply with the provisions in Section 1029 . 2. Curb ramps shall comply with ICC A117.1. 3. Vehicle ramps in parking garages for pedestrian exit access shall not be required to comply with Sections 1012.3 through 1012.10 where they are not an accessible route serving accessible parking spaces, other required accessible elements or part of an accessible means of egress.

1012.10 1012.10 Edge protection. Edge protection complying with Section 1012.10.1 shall be provided on each side of ramp runs and at each side of ramp landings not adjoining another ramp run or stairway. Exceptions: 1. Edge protection is not required on ramps that are not required to have handrails, provided they have flared sides that comply with the ICC A117.1 curb ramp provisions. 2. Edge protection is not required on the sides of ramp landings having a vertical dropoff of not more than 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) within 10 inches (254 mm) horizontally of the required landing area. 3. Edge protection is not required where the floor or ground surface of the ramp run or landing extends 12 inches (304.8 mm) minimum beyond the inside face of handrail complying with Section 1014 .

1012.8 1012.8 Handrails. Ramps with a rise greater than 6 inches (152.4 mm) shall have handrails on both sides. Handrails shall comply with Section 1014 . Exception: Handrails for ramped aisles are not required where permitted by Section 1029.15.

1012.5.1 1012.5.1 Width and capacity. The minimum width and required capacity of a means of egress ramp shall be not less than that required for corridors by Section 1020.2. The clear width of a ramp between handrails, if provided, or other permissible projections shall be 36 inches (914.4 mm) minimum.
1012.6 1012.6 Landings. Ramps shall have landings at the bottom and top of each ramp, points of turning, entrance, exits and at doors. Landings shall comply with Sections 1012.6.1 through 1012.6.5.
1012.3 1012.3 Cross slope. The slope measured perpendicular to the direction of travel of a ramp shall not be steeper than one unit vertical in 48 units horizontal (2-percent slope).
1012.7.1 1012.7.1 Ramp surface. The surface of ramps shall be of slip-resistant materials that are securely attached.
1012.4 1012.4 Vertical rise. The rise for any ramp run shall be 30 inches (762 mm) maximum.
1101.2 1101.2 Design. Buildings and facilities shall be designed and constructed to be accessible in accordance with ICC A117.1 and this code.

ACCESSIBLE. A site, building, facility or portion thereof that complies with Chapter 11 . ACCESSIBLE MEANS OF EGRESS. A continuous and unobstructed way of egress travel from any accessible point in a building or facility to a public way. Such way of egress travel may include an assisted rescue path. ACCESSIBLE ROUTE. A continuous, unobstructed path that complies with Chapter 11 . AISLE. An unenclosed exit access component that defines and provides a path of egress travel. EXIT ACCESS. That portion of a means of egress system that leads from any occupied portion of a building or structure to an exit. HANDRAIL. A horizontal or sloping rail intended for grasping by the hand for guidance or support. MEANS OF EGRESS. A continuous and unobstructed path of vertical and horizontal egress travel from any occupied portion of a building or structure to a public way. A means of egress consists of three separate and distinct parts: the exit access, the exit and the exit discharge. PARKING GARAGE. A structure or portion of a structure, other than a private garage or carport, used for the parking or storage of motor vehicles.
1012.5 1012.5 Minimum dimensions. The minimum dimensions of means of egress ramps shall comply with Sections 1012.5.1 through 1012.5.3.

1012.7 1012.7 Ramp construction. Ramps shall be built of materials consistent with the types permitted for the type of construction of the building, except that wood handrails shall be permitted for all types of construction.

1012.9 1012.9 Guards. Guards shall be provided where required by Section 1015 and shall be constructed in accordance with Section 1015. Such guards may be used to satisfy the requirement of edge protection of Section 1012.10.

1012.10.1 1012.10.1 Curb, rail, wall or barrier. A curb, rail, wall or barrier serving as edge protection shall be provided as follows: 1. Solid barriers. Solid barriers shall extend at least 4 inches (101.6 mm) from the floor or ground surface. 2. Other types of barriers. Other types of barriers shall prevent the passage of a 4-inch (101.6 mm) diameter sphere, where any portion of the sphere is within 4 inches (101.6 mm) of the floor or ground surface. Section BC 1013: Exit Signs
1012.6.1 1012.6.1 Slope. Landings shall have a slope not steeper than one unit vertical in 48 units horizontal (2-percent slope) in any direction. Changes in level are not permitted.
1012.6.5 1012.6.5 Doorways. Where doorways are located adjacent to a ramp landing, maneuvering clearances required by ICC A117.1 are permitted to overlap the required landing area.

answer.answerText:
**No.** On the stated facts, **1:8 does not comply**: a ramp used as part of a means of egress or an accessible route may not be steeper than **1:12 (8%)**. A 1:8 slope is 12.5%, so it exceeds that limit (BC § 1012.2).

The 1:8 maximum applies only to **“other pedestrian ramps.”** The stated ramp is neither a Group A aisle ramp nor a vehicle ramp, so neither special exception changes the result. The parking-garage vehicle-ramp exception applies only to specified provisions—BC §§ 1012.3 through 1012.10, not the slope limit in § 1012.2—and only where the ramp is not an accessible route serving the listed accessible elements and is not part of an accessible means of egress (BC § 1012.1).
answer.conclusion: **No.** On the stated facts, **1:8 does not comply**: a ramp used as part of a means of egress or an accessible route may not be steeper than **1:12 (8%)**. A 1:8 slope is 12.5%, so it exceeds that limit (BC § 1012.2).

supportedPoints.heading: Accessible means-of-egress ramp is limited to 1:12
supportedPoints.explanation: BC § 1012.2 requires ramps used as part of a means of egress or part of an accessible route to have a running slope no steeper than 1 vertical in 12 horizontal (8 percent). Because the stated ramp is part of an accessible means of egress, its 1:8 (12.5 percent) slope exceeds the applicable limit.

supportedPoints.heading: The vehicle-ramp exception does not change the slope limit
supportedPoints.explanation: The parking-garage vehicle-ramp exception applies only to BC §§ 1012.3 through 1012.10, not § 1012.2, and only where the vehicle ramp is not an accessible route serving the specified accessible elements and is not part of an accessible means of egress. The stated ordinary pedestrian ramp does not meet that subject matter.

supportedPoints.heading: Other directly supplied ramp rules remain separate
supportedPoints.explanation: The supplied provisions separately require a 1:48 maximum cross slope, 30-inch maximum rise for a ramp run, landings at listed locations, slip-resistant securely attached ramp surfaces, corridor-based width/capacity with 36 inches minimum clear width, handrails on both sides for rises greater than 6 inches subject to the stated ramped-aisle exception, and edge protection subject to listed exceptions. These rules do not relax the 1:12 running-slope limit.

supportedPoints.heading: Accessibility framework
supportedPoints.explanation: Buildings and facilities must be designed and constructed to be accessible in accordance with ICC A117.1 and the code. This provision does not alter the specific 1:12 maximum in BC § 1012.2.

sources.text: 1012.2 1012.2 Slope. Ramps used as part of a means of egress or part of an accessible route shall have a running slope not steeper than one unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (8-percent slope). The slope of other pedestrian ramps shall not be steeper than one unit vertical in eight units horizontal (12.5-percent slope). Exceptions: 1. Aisle ramp slope in occupancies of Group A shall comply with Section 1029.13. 2. In garages three stories or less in height and serving not more than one level below grade, ramps with a maximum slope of one unit vertical in seven units horizontal (14-percent slope) may serve as part of a nonaccessible means of egress.

1012.1 1012.1 Scope. The provisions of this section shall apply to ramps used as a component of a means of egress. Exceptions: 1. Other than ramps that are part of the accessible routes providing access in accordance with Sections 1108.2 through 1108.2.4 and 1108.2.6, ramped aisles within assembly rooms or spaces shall comply with the provisions in Section 1029 . 2. Curb ramps shall comply with ICC A117.1. 3. Vehicle ramps in parking garages for pedestrian exit access shall not be required to comply with Sections 1012.3 through 1012.10 where they are not an accessible route serving accessible parking spaces, other required accessible elements or part of an accessible means of egress.

1012.8 1012.8 Handrails. Ramps with a rise greater than 6 inches (152.4 mm) shall have handrails on both sides. Handrails shall comply with Section 1014 . Exception: Handrails for ramped aisles are not required where permitted by Section 1029.15.

1012.10 1012.10 Edge protection. Edge protection complying with Section 1012.10.1 shall be provided on each side of ramp runs and at each side of ramp landings not adjoining another ramp run or stairway. Exceptions: 1. Edge protection is not required on ramps that are not required to have handrails, provided they have flared sides that comply with the ICC A117.1 curb ramp provisions. 2. Edge protection is not required on the sides of ramp landings having a vertical dropoff of not more than 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) within 10 inches (254 mm) horizontally of the required landing area. 3. Edge protection is not required where the floor or ground surface of the ramp run or landing extends 12 inches (304.8 mm) minimum beyond the inside face of handrail complying with Section 1014 .

1012.5.1 1012.5.1 Width and capacity. The minimum width and required capacity of a means of egress ramp shall be not less than that required for corridors by Section 1020.2. The clear width of a ramp between handrails, if provided, or other permissible projections shall be 36 inches (914.4 mm) minimum.
1012.6 1012.6 Landings. Ramps shall have landings at the bottom and top of each ramp, points of turning, entrance, exits and at doors. Landings shall comply with Sections 1012.6.1 through 1012.6.5.
1012.3 1012.3 Cross slope. The slope measured perpendicular to the direction of travel of a ramp shall not be steeper than one unit vertical in 48 units horizontal (2-percent slope).
1012.7.1 1012.7.1 Ramp surface. The surface of ramps shall be of slip-resistant materials that are securely attached.
1012.4 1012.4 Vertical rise. The rise for any ramp run shall be 30 inches (762 mm) maximum.
1101.2 1101.2 Design. Buildings and facilities shall be designed and constructed to be accessible in accordance with ICC A117.1 and this code.

ACCESSIBLE. A site, building, facility or portion thereof that complies with Chapter 11 . ACCESSIBLE MEANS OF EGRESS. A continuous and unobstructed way of egress travel from any accessible point in a building or facility to a public way. Such way of egress travel may include an assisted rescue path. ACCESSIBLE ROUTE. A continuous, unobstructed path that complies with Chapter 11 . AISLE. An unenclosed exit access component that defines and provides a path of egress travel. EXIT ACCESS. That portion of a means of egress system that leads from any occupied portion of a building or structure to an exit. HANDRAIL. A horizontal or sloping rail intended for grasping by the hand for guidance or support. MEANS OF EGRESS. A continuous and unobstructed path of vertical and horizontal egress travel from any occupied portion of a building or structure to a public way. A means of egress consists of three separate and distinct parts: the exit access, the exit and the exit discharge. PARKING GARAGE. A structure or portion of a structure, other than a private garage or carport, used for the parking or storage of motor vehicles.
1012.5 1012.5 Minimum dimensions. The minimum dimensions of means of egress ramps shall comply with Sections 1012.5.1 through 1012.5.3.

1012.7 1012.7 Ramp construction. Ramps shall be built of materials consistent with the types permitted for the type of construction of the building, except that wood handrails shall be permitted for all types of construction.

1012.9 1012.9 Guards. Guards shall be provided where required by Section 1015 and shall be constructed in accordance with Section 1015. Such guards may be used to satisfy the requirement of edge protection of Section 1012.10.

1012.10.1 1012.10.1 Curb, rail, wall or barrier. A curb, rail, wall or barrier serving as edge protection shall be provided as follows: 1. Solid barriers. Solid barriers shall extend at least 4 inches (101.6 mm) from the floor or ground surface. 2. Other types of barriers. Other types of barriers shall prevent the passage of a 4-inch (101.6 mm) diameter sphere, where any portion of the sphere is within 4 inches (101.6 mm) of the floor or ground surface. Section BC 1013: Exit Signs
1012.6.1 1012.6.1 Slope. Landings shall have a slope not steeper than one unit vertical in 48 units horizontal (2-percent slope) in any direction. Changes in level are not permitted.
1012.6.5 1012.6.5 Doorways. Where doorways are located adjacent to a ramp landing, maneuvering clearances required by ICC A117.1 are permitted to overlap the required landing area.
